Thisis a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA)between the153AW and theCPD.When referred
to collectively, the153AWand theCPD are referred to as the“Parties".
BACKGROUND:153SF S has limited law enforcement authority and acts principally to protect
military assets and personnel essential for National Defense.This MOA acknowledges thatinsome
situations theremay be no practical distinction between threats to the area and to Defense assets and
provides the mechanism by which acertified law enforcement official of theCPDmay request 153SFS
response to contingencies.The Governor of Wyoming or hislawful designee will determine the
availability and extent of direct assistance to law enforcement that the153AWwill provide.
Additionally, thisMOA addresses shared law enforcement responsibilities for situations arising on
Wyoming Military Department property located at 217Dell Range Boulevard, Cheyenne, Wyoming
82009.
2.AUTHORITIES: In accordance with DoD Instruction 2000.16 v1, Anti terrorism (AT) Program
and Air Force Instruction(AF1)10-245, Air Force AT Standards, andAFI25-201, Intra-Service, Intra-
Agency, and Inter-Agency Support Agreement Procedures, this Memorandum of Agreement(MOA)
coordinates emergency services by and between the153 AW, Wyoming Air National Guard and
Cheyenne Police Department (CPD) in their efforts to supply the residents of the respective jurisdictions
with protection from natural and manmade disasters, crime or acts of terrorism.
3.
PURPOSE: The153 AW and the CPD acknowledge that a situation could arise that may require
armed support in cooperation with local law enforcement agencies.
AGREEMENTS OF THE PARTIES: Therefore, the153AWand the CP D agree to mutually
practice crisis management which shall include measures to identify, acquire, and plan the use of
resources needed to anticipate, prevent, and/or resolve a natural or manmade disaster(s), criminal acts or
acts of terrorism.
4.1.153d Security Forces Squadron(153SFS)will—
4.1.1 Provide armed response to all suspicious activities on the Cheyenne Airport
property located within the perimeter fence line (excluding buildings such as the terminal
andhangers).
4.1.2.Share pertinent intelligence with CPD.153 SFS will exchange intelligence and law
enforcement sensitive information via email and/or Facsimile(FAX).

4.1.2.1.153SFS will immediately notify CPD of suspicious incidents/vehicles
and suspicious activity, including incident near the perimeter of theWYANG
Base or adjacent areas, via direct landline to the Laramie County Combined
Dispatch Center.
4.2.Cheyenne Police Department(CPD)will—
4.2.1.Provide armed response for the investigation of crimes committed on theWYANG
Base and remote locations. CPD will, as appropriate, arrest individuals
detained/apprehended by the153d Security Forces Squadron(153SFS)onthe153AW.
4.2.2.Provide armed response to the 153 AWfor terrorist incident, active shooter,
Explosive Detection/Disposal support, Explosive/Narcotics Detector Dog support, CPD
Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT)and or Hostage Negotiation Team (HNT) support
as deemed appropriated by responding CP D personnel.
4.2.3.Participate in 153AW Threat Working Group meetings as needed.
4.2.4.Share pertinent intelligence with 153 SFS.CPDwill exchange intelligence and
law enforcement sensitive information via email and/or Facsimile(FAX).
4.2.4.1.CPDwill immediately notify153SFSof suspicious incidents/vehicles
and suspicious activity via direct landline to the153AWBD0C at772-6309.
4.2.5.In situations where CPD wishes to request use of 153SFS assets, they may make
the request through the Adjutant General Joint Operations Center(JOC) at 307-772-5112.
5.PERSONNEL: Each Party is responsible for all costs of its personnel, including pay and
benefits, support, and travel.Each Party is responsible for supervision and management ofits personnel.

6.3.FUNDS AND MANPOWER: This MOA does not document nor provide for the exchange
of funds or manpower between the Parties nor does it make any commitment of funds or

6.4.MODIFICATION OFMOA: ThisMOA may only be modified by the written agreement of
the Parties, duly signed by their authorized representatives.This MOA will be reviewed annually
on or around the anniversary of its effective date, and triennially in its entirety.

6.5. DISPUTES: Any disputes relating to the interpretation and/or performance of this agreement
will be determined according to this paragraph. If there is a dispute in interpretation and/or
performance under this agreement arisingfrom and primarily concerning theWYANG premises
or operations or anincident which constitutes animminent threat to theWYANG premises,
equipment or operations, the W YANG Commanders hall havefinal authority with the advice and
assistance of the relevant CPD personnel. The CPD shall have final authority as to disputes
concerning all other airport matters and locations subject to applicable state orfederal law and
Executive Order, Directive or Instruction, andmay be mutually resolved through consultation
between the parties in accordance with DoDI4000.19 andAFI25-201, para3.6.
by either Party.
